desc: Ideation: select iterative BFS/DFS integer-potential approach as primary, with bitwise per-component majority mask.

Implement the complete Python program using the iterative DFS integer-potential approach: read N, M and all edges into an adjacency list; for each unvisited vertex, run an iterative stack DFS assigning potentials (root potential 0) and check every edge for `pot[u] ^ pot[v] == z`; if any violation, print `-1`; otherwise for each component count set bits among its vertex potentials for bits `0..30` (or `0..max(1, max_z.bit_length())`), set the component mask bit to 1 iff the count is greater than `len(component)//2`, and set `A[v] = pot[v] ^ mask`; finally print `A[1..N]`. Include self-loop and parallel-edge handling, avoid recursion, and enclose the code in the required delimiters.
Run the implementation on the provided samples and edge cases (M=0, self-loop with z=0 and z!=0, inconsistent cycle, large chain) and fix any failures.
